summary: Partial output on SSE resume after reverse-proxy HTTP/2->1.1 rewrite causes terminal fragment loss
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after an SSE (Server-Sent Events) reconnect behind their corporate reverse proxy, the final/terminal choice for responses is missing or truncated. The client sees a resume stream but the last token(s) are not delivered, leading to semantically incomplete replies.

Impact:
- A BrightHealth AI production integration (enterprise tier) in eu-west intermittently receives incomplete model outputs for streaming chat flows.
- Impacts user-facing sessions (billing continues) and causes downstream application logic to treat responses as failed, triggering retries.
- Reported frequency: ~1-3% of long streams (>800 tokens) in peak hours.

Environment:
- Customer environment: corporate reverse proxy in front of Redwood API (NGINX ingress acting as HTTP/2 terminator, rewrites to HTTP/1.1 to backend).
- Redwood side: hosted inference in prod | eu-west, API gateway + serving-runtime.
- Client platform: browser webapp and server-side long-polling consumer.

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Initiate a streaming chat generation request against Redwood API with a long completion (approx. 1k tokens) via browser behind corporate proxy.
2) During generation introduce a short network hiccup to the client (simulate reload or transient network drop).
3) Client reconnects using session resume token; server accepts resume and emits buffered fragments.
4) Observe that in ~2 out of 10 replays the final "end" fragment (terminal choice) is missing or cut mid-token.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should replay fragments and emit a complete terminal event containing final tokens and metadata (e.g., choice.complete = true).

Observed behavior:
- The stream resumes and sends the majority of fragments but the terminal fragment is either truncated (partial UTF-8 sequence / partial JSON) or not emitted at all. Client-side reassembly yields broken JSON or incomplete sentence.
- No 5xx from Redwood; proxy logs show 200 but with truncated content-length/chunking patterns.

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- Client SSE recv logs show sequence: CHUNK(123) CHUNK(456) ... CHUNK(EOF-MISSING)
- NGINX proxy access log: backend_time=0.241 upstream_status=200 upstream_bytes=16384 request_length=...
- TCP trace between client and proxy shows HTTP/2 stream reset around resume window.
- Upstream (Redwood) app logs: "stream: resume accepted for session=brt-XXXXX, dispatched 17 chunks" (no explicit terminal error).

Initial hypothesis:
- The proxy performs an HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 rewrite and aggressively buffers or rewrites chunked bodies; the trailing chunk that contains the SSE terminal event gets coalesced/stripped by the proxy layer during reconnect path. Alternatively, HTTP/2 flow control reset during resume results in the final chunk being dropped between proxy and client.

References:
- Slack: #support (thread ts: 1643321) and #infra (ts: 1643456)
- Customer repro gist (sanitized): https://gist.github.com/brighthealthai/sse-repro

Workaround requested by customer:
- Preferable short-term: ask customer to set proxy config to disable response buffering for the SSE route: proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on.
- Fallback: advise client to detect truncated final JSON and re-request last N tokens via non-streaming endpoint as a patch.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:08 - Asha Patel (Support): Logged by BrightHealth AI. Customer reports partial terminal tokens only on resume behind corporate proxy. Asked for traces and proxy config.

2026-03-10 11:22 - BrightHealth AI (Customer): We see it on both browser and server consumers. Proxy is NGINX ingress (k8s) with HTTP/2 front, rewrite to 1.1 to backend. We can reproduce reliably when a reconnect happens during last 50 tokens of a long response.

2026-03-10 14:03 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Ran quick repro from eu-west lambda through a test NGINX with same settings. Observed identical truncated last fragment when proxy had proxy_buffering enabled. When turned off, terminal fragment arrived consistently.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Marta Ruiz (Runtime Eng): Created debug build to log terminal fragment emission and added sequence IDs to SSE framing. Logs on Redwood side show terminal fragment emitted in full to upstream pipe; likely mid-path loss.

2026-03-11 15:42 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Proposed temporary mitigation: add short-lived API header X-Stream-No-Buffer=true to force gateway to set no-buffering on upstream routes. Not ideal but can be rolled quickly for affected customer.

2026-03-12 08:00 - BrightHealth AI (Customer): Applied proxy_buffering off for SSE route and reports no truncated streams in 24h stress test. Reverting shows the issue returns. Customer will coordinate with their infra team to keep change while we investigate a robust fix.

2026-03-12 12:15 - Marta Ruiz (Runtime Eng): Opening PR to emit an explicit SSE 'terminal-marker' event in addition to current terminal payload (adds redundancy for proxies that drop final chunk): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/12840
investigation_notes: Repro on internal testbed using customer's NGINX config reproduced the issue. When NGINX proxy_buffering was enabled, the final chunk often did not reach client after resume. With proxy_buffering off and proxy_http_version 1.1 the terminal event consistently arrived. Server logs show terminal payload written and flushed; no application-side exception. Hypothesis strengthened: buffering + HTTP/2 rewrite + resume flow control interaction are the root cause. Further tests show Envoy with HTTP/2 passthrough behaves correctly, suggesting this is specific to certain ingress rewrites that coalesce/truncate last chunk on reconnects.
resolution:
Temporary: Instructed customer to set proxy buffering off for SSE endpoints and provided header workaround (X-Stream-No-Buffer=true). Customer applied change and confirmed regression disappeared in immediate tests.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Short-term (ENG): Merge PR to emit a redundant explicit 'terminal-marker' SSE event after the normal end-of-stream payload to tolerate dropped last chunk (PR #12840).
- Mid-term (INFRA): Add gateway rule to set no-buffering for streaming routes by default and propagate to Dedicated/Private docs.
- Long-term (ARCH): Investigate more robust resume ack flow that confirms terminal event receipt; evaluate end-to-end sequence ACKs for streaming sessions.

Follow-ups:
- Track rollout of PR 12840 and run e2e tests via customer NGINX config.
- Create KB article for customers describing required proxy settings for SSE streaming.
- Link ticket to infra policy change (internal task).
notes: Customer verified workaround in production: proxy_buffering off for SSE path
PR opened: serving-runtime will emit redundant terminal marker
Next step: infra to add default streaming route flags and update docs
